# Part II: Generative and Multimodal Architectures {#part-generative .unnumbered}

> "Learning directly from raw text about images is a promising alternative."
>
> Alec Radford et al., ["Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020)

Part I built the machinery for a model that consumes tokens. This part steps off
the main text-model spine to follow a parallel track: generation when the object
is not naturally a left-to-right string. Images, audio, video, speech, and
embodied observations all raise the same problem: the model must make something
coherent, but the thing being made may not have a single natural order. The
autoregressive language model resumes its lifecycle in Part III; the
architectures here developed alongside it and do not replace it.

Part II follows the architectures developed in response to that problem. It
opens in @sec-diffusion with denoising and flow matching, where generation is
learned as a path from noise to structure rather than as the next token in a
sequence. The same problem returns to language in @sec-nar-lm, which asks what
non-autoregressive and diffusion language models gain, and what they lose when
they give up the cache and the simple serving path of autoregressive decoding.
@sec-speech and @sec-multimodal then move through speech recognition, speech
generation, vision-language fusion, image generation, and video. By
@sec-beyond-text the scope widens to world models, robotics, and embodiment,
where the bottleneck is often a reliable stream of experience grounded in the
physical world rather than model size.

Each chapter of this part, whether it covers images, audio, or robots, examines
the sequence a system constructs over its output so that training, caching,
sampling, and evaluation become possible. That invented order is the
architecture.
